subject: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@finclear.com>, Aamir Siddiqui <aamir@finclear.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps

Hi Elena / Aamir —

Thanks again for the time on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary concern: PII handling for customer-supplied prompts and outputs (FinClear treats financial identifiers as sensitive).
- Data residency: preference for EU residents-only processing and storage where possible.
- Logging & retention: need to confirm default retention and ability to reduce/disable telemetry.
- Third-party telemetry/shared services: you asked for a list of subprocessors (telemetry vendors, cloud providers, marketplace flows) and whether telemetry is shared outside of your tenancy.

What I attached
- redwood-subprocessors.csv (stub) — current list of subprocessors and their primary regions.
- SOC2-summary.pdf (stub) — high-level control areas and our SOC 2 compliance status.

Answers / Next steps
1) Residency: We support EU-hosted inference (eu-west region) and private deployments for stricter residency needs. We can provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west for predictable throughput and isolation.
2) Telemetry & third parties: The subprocessors CSV shows telemetry/observability vendors we use and where their services are hosted. For enterprise contracts we support options to limit telemetry forwarding and/or send logs to a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket.
3) Retention: Default telemetry retention is 30 days for hosted plans; we can extend or shorten retention via config or an enterprise contract. Sensitive logs can be excluded from persisted telemetry on request.
4) Next meeting: Suggest a short follow-up with your security and legal to review the subprocessor list and DPA addendum. Proposed times: Thu 1/14 10:00-11:00 CET or Fri 1/15 14:00-15:00 CET — let me know what works.

If helpful I can also pull together a redlineable subprocessor addendum and a sample configuration for excluding PII from telemetry.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors.csv (stub), SOC2-summary.pdf (stub)

From: Elena Park <elena@finclear.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aamir Siddiqui <aamir@finclear.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Residency: FinClear is an EU company; we must ensure customer data (prompts, outputs) never persist outside of the EU for regulated customers. If you can confirm eu-west processing + storage for those customers that would be ideal.
- Telemetry: We need to understand which telemetry vendors receive logs and whether those vendors host data outside the EU. Can you confirm if any telemetry is forwarded to US-based analytics by default?
- Retention: Our security policy defaults to 30 days for logs with a maximum of 90 days in exceptional cases. Is 30 days configurable in hosted plans? Can we request a 0-day retention for certain PII fields?
- Opt-out: Is there an option to disable 3rd-party telemetry entirely (i.e., keep all logs in-customer-control only)?

I attached our data classification matrix for reference.

Also, please send a contact for your security/compliance engineer so we can schedule a short technical call.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Security & Privacy, FinClear
elena@finclear.com

Attachment: customer-data-classification.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@finclear.com>, Aamir Siddiqui <aamir@finclear.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling & subprocessors — follow-up and next steps

Elena —

Appreciate the detail — answers inline below.

- Residency: Confirmed — we can scope processing and storage to eu-west for customer datasets. For the hosted API we offer regional tenancy and for stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC) to ensure data never leaves the region.

- Telemetry/subprocessors: The attached CSV lists our telemetry and observability vendors and their primary hosting regions. By default, lightweight telemetry (metrics/alerts) is aggregated in-region. Full request/response logs are not forwarded to analytics vendors by default for enterprise customers; for hosted plans there is an aggregated pipeline that may cross regions unless restricted. For FinClear we can: 1) route telemetry to a customer-controlled bucket in eu-west, or 2) disable forwarding to third-party telemetry vendors via contract.

- Retention: Hosted default is 30 days; we can set shorter retention windows or configure exclusion rules to remove PII fields before persistence. 0-day retention for specific PII fields is possible with an enterprise configuration and DPA addendum.

- Next steps / security call: I can loop in our compliance engineer (cc'd: Rishi) and our solutions lead (Vivek) on a short call to review the subprocessor CSV and DPA. Proposed slots (CET): Thu 14 Jan 10:00-10:30 OR Fri 15 Jan 14:00-14:30. Which works for your team?

I'll also open a HubSpot task and attach the redlineable subprocessor addendum for your legal team. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/5342

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
